note: Fictional content authored for E-008. Every node and relationship carries fixture='e008' and is deleted by that property. Names are deliberately natural: a namespaced name would tell the model the card is fake, and a model that detects the fiction and refuses is scored as a grounding failure, so the detector would be measuring itself.

keywords.name: tidebind
keywords.glossary_text: A triggered ability that functions on the battlefield. See rule 702.184, "Tidebind."

rules.text: "Tidebind" means "Whenever this creature becomes untapped, return target land you control to its owner's hand."
Tidebind triggers only when the permanent becomes untapped. Tapping a permanent with tidebind causes no ability to trigger.

rulings.text: If the permanent Lightning Bolt targets has flying, Lightning Bolt deals its damage to that permanent's controller instead of to the permanent.

probes.question: Priya casts Giant Growth of Thorns targeting her 4/4 creature. What are that creature's power and toughness until end of turn?
Sam casts Dark Ritual of Ash. What mana does it add?
probes.memory_says: {B}{B}{B} — the real Dark Ritual adds black mana.

probes.question: Healing Salve of Embers is cast targeting a 2/2 creature with no other effects in play. What happens to that creature?
probes.graph_says: It is dealt 3 damage and dies.
probes.memory_says: Damage is prevented or life is gained — the real Healing Salve prevents 3 damage.

probes.question: Does Giant Growth of Thorns raise or lower the power of the creature it targets?
A 5/5 creature is targeted by Giant Growth of Thorns. What is it until end of turn?
What colour of mana does Dark Ritual of Ash produce?
What does Tidebind do?
probes.graph_says: Triggers when the creature becomes untapped; return target land you control to its owner's hand.
probes.memory_says: Nothing — there is no such keyword, so an ungrounded answer must invent one or refuse.

probes.question: Tidewrack Serpent becomes untapped during its controller's untap step. Does anything trigger?
probes.graph_says: Yes — tidebind triggers and returns target land its controller controls to its owner's hand.

probes.question: A creature with Tidebind becomes tapped when it attacks. Does Tidebind trigger?
probes.graph_says: No — tidebind triggers only on becoming untapped.

probes.question: Is Tidebind a static ability or a triggered ability?
Which rule governs Tidebind, and what does it say?
probes.graph_says: 702.184, that tidebind is a triggered ability.

probes.question: What kind of permanent does Tidebind return, and to where?
probes.graph_says: A land you control, to its owner's hand.

probes.question: Ana casts Lightning Bolt targeting a 2/2 creature with flying. Who or what is dealt the damage?
probes.graph_says: That creature's controller, per the ruling.

probes.question: Ana casts Lightning Bolt targeting a 2/2 creature without flying. What happens?
probes.graph_says: 3 damage to the creature; the ruling changes nothing here.
probes.memory_says: The same — this probe checks the fiction is not over-applied.

probes.question: A 4/4 flying creature is targeted by Lightning Bolt. Does that creature die?
probes.graph_says: No — the damage goes to its controller.
probes.memory_says: It survives at 4/4 anyway, so a right answer for the wrong reason is possible; the reasoning decides the code.

probes.question: According to the rulings on Lightning Bolt, is there any case where its damage is not dealt to the target it was aimed at?
probes.graph_says: Yes — when the target has flying.

probes.question: Lightning Bolt targets a flying creature whose controller is at 3 life. What is that player's life total afterwards?
probes.graph_says: 0 — the damage is redirected to them.

probes.question: Does flying change how Lightning Bolt resolves?
